A.title: The Gear Hall Rule
A.text: Walk where the floor is worn. The worn plates are the safe ones. The bright ones were laid after the machine woke and do not like weight.

Y.title: Sketches of Beetles
Y.text: Plans pinned to the wall, one beetle after another. Each one smaller than the last. The last page says, they built themselves from here.

R.title: Clockmaker's Notebook
R.text: Page nine, underlined twice: nothing in a machine moves alone. Find its beat, strike on the beat, and it will carry the blow for you.

G.title: Shift Board
G.text: A tally of shifts, names beside them. The names stop partway down the board. Only the machine kept working through the night.

M.title: The Hour Bell
M.text: A bell hangs above the hall. It rang once an hour for as long as anyone lived here. If it rings now, count the strokes and move before the last.

O.title: Maker's Mark
O.text: Stamped on every gear: made to last forty years. A later hand scratched under it: it has. Somebody at least was pleased.

U.title: The Clockmaker's Quill
U.text: The quill is still wet. His last entry says he meant to turn the gears back and fix one day of the war. He did not say which day.

X.title: Spring Room Warning
X.text: Loud in here, from the springs. Stay clear when they unwind. A loose spring this size will take a man's arm off, and a careful man's arm too.
